title: Sable and the Deadline
premise: Casper Okafor, a freelance interpreter who built her career on being unattributable, is attached to a fragile three-party peace delegation when Flight 4471—carrying a witness to the delegation's darkest secret—vanishes from every radar, manifest, and memory mid-flight. As Casper reconstructs the flight from fragments lodged in her own interpreted notes, she realizes the erasure was negotiated, not accidental, and that her invisibility makes her the only person alive who can testify. Hunted by an assassin who once spared her and pressured by the governments she serves, she smuggles the truth out through the one channel no one polices: simultaneous interpretation itself. The book ends with Casper choosing truth over belonging, broadcasting the erased flight live to all three delegations at once, surviving the assassin's final mercy, and walking away stateless but unowned.
about_author: Mara Halloran spent a decade working behind glass in conference booths across four continents before turning to fiction, and her thrillers are prized for their insider texture of diplomacy's back rooms. She writes under a pen name because, as she puts it, some stories can only be told by someone with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Booth
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Arriving at the Geneva summit, Casper establishes her craft and her creed: interpreters hear everything and belong nowhere. She notices the delegation's security chief quietly pulling files on her. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness; she has made invisibility an art and believes it keeps her safe.

chapters.title: Three Flags, One Table
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Opening sessions collapse into mutual accusation over a downed aid corridor. Casper renders each side's insults faithfully, earning a flicker of respect from the assassin-adjacent security detail. A delegate named Ilse Voss slips her a note: 'Listen for what isn't said.' Emotional beat: the intoxicating, dangerous intimacy of knowing everyone's secrets.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A chartered flight carrying Voss's star witness—a logistics officer with proof of a sanctioned massacre—takes off for Geneva. Casper interprets the delegation's tense phone call authorizing its approach. Then, mid-sentence, the tower line goes dead. Emotional beat: dread arriving before understanding; the silence feels wrong in a way only she registers.

chapters.title: Nothing in the Air
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. No crash site, no manifest, no passenger list—the flight never existed. Delegations deny it ever departed. Casper checks her own booth recordings: wiped. Only her handwritten glossary notes survive, fragments of the authorization call. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo; the ground itself seems unreliable.

chapters.title: What the Notes Remember
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Reconstructing the call from shorthand, Casper confirms the flight was real and that someone with summit authority ordered it 'handled.' She realizes her notes are now the only record on earth. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; invisibility has become evidence.

chapters.title: The Man Who Spared Her
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. In a hotel stairwell she meets Davor Renko, the summit's fixer—an assassin she encountered years ago in Sarajevo who let her walk away. He warns her, gently, to forget the flight. His mercy then is a debt now. Emotional beat: terror braided with strange tenderness.

chapters.title: Ilse's Room
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Voss admits she sent the witness and confesses her government will disown both of them. She gives Casper a dead-drop protocol and a name: the Deputy who brokered the erasure. That night Voss's room burns. Emotional beat: grief and guilt; every ally Casper touches becomes kindling.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Summit security brands Voss's death accidental and Casper a person of interest. Her accreditation is revoked mid-shift; she interprets her own expulsion through the booth glass. Emotional beat: public unmasking—the invisibility she cultivated turns into a target painted on her back.

chapters.title: Stateless
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Hiding in the migrant quarter, Casper confronts her own history: a childhood of borrowed languages and borrowed countries, no passport that truly fits. A local fixer, Amara, shelters her. Emotional beat: the theme of belonging turned inward; she must decide what she owes a world that never claimed her.

chapters.title: Renko's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Renko finds her—not to kill her but to show her his contract: three governments co-signed the erasure, and his employer wants her notes destroyed and her death deniable. He offers her forty-eight hours before he's obligated to act. Emotional beat: a countdown begins; mercy with an expiry date.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Using an old booth contact, Casper gets ten minutes interpreting for the Deputy's private call—and hears him rehearse the same lies she transcribed from the vanished flight. Her earprint memory becomes forensic proof. Emotional beat: cold triumph curdling into horror at how high the rot goes.

chapters.title: Amara's Price
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Amara's network agrees to move Casper's copied notes across borders—but demands she interpret for a debt-collection meeting between rival smugglers, risking exposure. She does it flawlessly and hates herself for how good it feels. Emotional beat: complicity; survival always costs someone else something.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The note courier is taken at the border; the copies burn. Security now knows exactly where Casper slept last night. Renko arrives seconds ahead of the kill team and gets her out, breaking his contract's letter if not its spirit. Emotional beat: betrayal of every institution; trust narrows to one dangerous man.

chapters.title: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. On a freight barge, Casper and Renko plan the impossible: get the truth inside the closing plenary where all three governments sit together, on the record, with press present. Her only weapon is the interpreter's chair itself. Emotional beat: desperate clarity; the deadline stops being a threat and becomes a design.

chapters.title: The Earprint
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Flashbacks interleave with preparation: how Casper trained herself to hold voices whole, why she fled Sarajevo, what Renko's old mercy really cost him. They forge accreditation using Voss's hidden credentials. Emotional beat: memory as inheritance; the past stops haunting and starts arming her.

chapters.title: Closed Session
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Smuggled in as a substitute linguist, Casper interprets the closed session where the three governments finalize the cover story she knows is false. She renders their lies perfectly into all three languages—while recording. Renko stands guard outside. Emotional beat: white-knuckle poise; her greatest professional performance is also her treason.

chapters.title: Renko's Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. His employers confirm the order: finish it tonight. Renko tells Casper he won't—but his second, a true believer, will. They split up so the kill team follows Renko. Emotional beat: sacrifice without romance; he gives her the head start he once gave her in Sarajevo, knowingly spending himself.

chapters.title: The Plenary Floor
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Final day. Accredited at the last moment through a sympathetic booth veteran, Casper takes the plenary interpretation seat as the closing communiqué is read. The Deputy watches her like a man watching weather turn. Emotional beat: terrible calm; the booth glass is both shield and confession box.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. When the communiqué denies Flight 4471 ever existed, Casper breaks protocol: instead of translating the lie, she broadcasts the Deputy's own recorded voice—his rehearsed denial, timestamped—in all three languages, live, to every delegate and open mic. The hall detonates. Emotional beat: catharsis; the invisible woman makes three governments listen to themselves.

chapters.title: What Follows the Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Chaos: walkouts, a deputy arrested mid-corridor, delegates demanding the flight's records be reopened. The believer-hunter corners Casper backstage; Renko arrives bleeding and ends it, taking a wound meant for her. Emotional beat: violence as punctuation, not solution; the truth is out but bodies still break.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Under inquiry, Casper testifies with her notes, her memory, and the recording—refusing anonymity, signing her name for the first time in her career. The flight's passengers are posthumously acknowledged; the massacre investigation reopens. Emotional beat: mourning and vindication entwined; visibility hurts exactly as much as promised.

chapters.title: No Attribution Required
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Offered citizenship, contracts, a podium, Casper declines them all. She visits Voss's grave, leaves her glossary notebook there, and meets Renko one last time at a border neither will name. She walks through alone, unrecorded by choice. Emotional beat: quiet freedom; belonging, she finally understands, is something you carry, not something you're granted.
